chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hadeed ibn Hakim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The least of ingratitude is the saying 'Uff' (a slight exhalation of impatience), and had Allah, Mighty and Majestic, known of anything lighter than it, He would have forbidden it.

key_terms.أُفٍّ: A slight sound of impatience or exhalation

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum act of disrespect towards parents in Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith establishes 'Uff'—a soft sigh of impatience—as the baseline for parental ingratitude, illustrating that even minor signs of annoyance constitute a breach of respect. The Prophet’s or Imam’s assertion that God would have prohibited something lighter if possible underscores the gravity of this single syllable, elevating it from mere rudeness to a spiritual deficiency. This aligns with the Shia emphasis on adab (etiquette) as an integral component of faith, where internal states manifest in subtle external actions.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Hadeed Bin Hakeym, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The least of the ingratitude is (the saying of) ‘Ugh’, and had Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Known of anything lesser than it, He<sup>azwj</sup> would have Forbidden from it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Hadid ibn Hakim from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Minimum of al-‘Uquq, (to cause disappointment) is to say ‘Uff (expression of disapproval). Had Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, known anything expressing a lesser degree of disappointment than this ‘Uff, He would have prohibited it.”
